en.title: Joe Manganiello's Dragonlance Dream Lives On: 'Never Give Up Hope'
en.summary: Despite his ambitious Dragonlance TV series being shelved years ago, Joe Manganiello remains optimistic about bringing the beloved D&D world to the screen. He shared insights into the project's past struggles and his enduring passion for the project.
en.body:
For years, fans have lamented the cancellation of Joe Manganiello's planned **Dragonlance** TV series, a project that held immense promise for bringing the iconic D&D setting to live-action. However, the actor and passionate gamer has revealed that his hope for the show is far from extinguished.

Speaking at **Lucca Comics and Games 2026**, Manganiello detailed the five years of work poured into the project, which ultimately stalled due to behind-the-scenes leadership changes at Entertainment One. He explained how key supporters departed, leaving the **Dragonlance** series and a related documentary in a precarious position. "When both of those got put on the shelf due to a change of leadership – due to shuffling going on within [Entertainment One] – those projects became nobody's child," Manganiello stated. He elaborated on how his initial champion, Michael Lombardo, who understood his vision, was no longer there when critical development stages were reached, leaving him without crucial allies. "He's my guy. He's the guy who understood my pitch. He's the one who believed in me. He's the one who saw what it could be, and he's gone," he shared.

## A Community's Lingering Hope

The news that Manganiello still holds out hope for **Dragonlance** will undoubtedly energize the dedicated D&D community. The **Dragonlance** saga, featuring iconic characters like Raistlin Majere and the Heroes of the Lance, is a foundational text for many who discovered role-playing games in the 1980s and 90s. The potential for a faithful adaptation, spearheaded by someone as deeply invested as Manganiello, has always been a dream for fans. His continued advocacy suggests that the dream isn't dead, merely dormant, and that there's a significant audience eager to see it revived.

## What's Next for the Dragonborn

While the **Dragonlance** TV series remains in limbo, Manganiello hinted that a documentary project with Danny Ayoub might be closer to realization. However, specific details regarding any renewed development on the **Dragonlance** television show, including potential new partners or a revised timeline, have not yet been announced. Manganiello's persistent optimism, however, leaves the door open for future possibilities.

content_raw: Joe Manganiello, one of the most famous Dungeons & Dragons players in Hollywood, said he still wants his Dragonlance TV series to come to fruition despite its cancellation several years ago. The Justice League and One Piece actor was hired as showrunner and screenwriter on the show years ago, promising a live-action adaptation of one of the stories that helped introduce him to tabletop role-playing. After a series of snags, though, Manganiello eventually went on to confirm that his live-action Dragonlance would no longer come to be. IGN asked Manganiello about his ill-fated D&D project during a conversation at Lucca Comics and Games 2026. He walked us through how, after five years of work, things fell apart, while also teasing that the door for a Dragonlance TV show – and even his documentary – will never close. "When both of those got put on the shelf due to a change of leadership – due to shuffling going on within [Entertainment One] – those projects became nobody's child," he explained. "I mean, I was hired by Michael Lombardo, who was my old boss at HBO. He hired me to create a television show, to create the next Game of Thrones for him, but then he was gone. "He's my guy. He's the guy who understood my pitch. He's the one who believed in me. He's the one who saw what it could be, and he's gone. And then, my other producing partner, he was gone, too. So, the two people that I was there with are gone, and the people there had different ideas. All of a sudden, those things become the priority as I'm turning in my script. Now, my people aren't there. Same with the documentary." Manganiello went on to say that, as his hands-on time in the D&D universe began to fall apart, he had "nobody helping to fight with" him to bring then-in-development projects to life. With Dragonlance officially confirmed to be canned in 2024, it was around this time the actor thought "OK, I'm out," but as he told us, "there is new hope." "[President of Wizards of the Coast & Hasbro Digital Games] Dan Ayoub is a fantastic leader. He gets it, and we work really well together," he continued. "I think there are talented people within the building now that are doing some amazing things, and we're going to do some amazing things together. "The dream was always, always to be off running a Dragonlance series, and I will never give up hope on that. And I think there's a lot of people that share that vision. I think the documentary with Danny Ayoub is actually going to be closer to getting out as well." That's two big updates on two D&D projects that many fans believed were destined to never see the light of day. Still, as the pieces move into place on the board behind the scenes, it's best not to get hopes up too high until Manganiello and the rest of his team have more to announce. For example, Ayoub took up his position as president just four days ago after previously serving as senior vice president of Dungeons & Dragons.
